coding.title: Group anagrams
coding.prompt: Given an array of strings, group the anagrams together. Return the groups in any order.
coding.hint: Create a canonical signature for each word, such as a 26-letter frequency tuple.

concept.title: A shared signature finds the group
concept.summary: Anagrams contain the same letters with the same counts. Turn each word into a stable key, then use that key to collect matching words.

steps.label: Count letters
steps.detail: For “eat”, count one a, one e, and one t. Letter order no longer matters.

steps.label: Build a key
steps.detail: The sorted letters make a canonical signature: aet. “tea” and “ate” produce the same key.

steps.label: Collect matches
steps.detail: Append each word to the bucket for its signature, then return the buckets.

coding.title: Longest substring without repeats
coding.prompt: Return the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
coding.hint: Keep a moving window and the last seen index of each character.

concept.title: Move a window as characters arrive
concept.summary: Keep a window with no repeated characters. When the right edge finds a duplicate, move the left edge just past its previous position.

steps.label: Start the window
steps.detail: Read a, b, c. The current window is “abc”, length 3.

steps.label: See a duplicate
steps.detail: The next a repeats. Move the left edge past the old a; the valid window becomes “bca”.

steps.label: Keep scanning
steps.detail: Track the largest valid window seen. Later repeats shrink the window without losing the best answer.

coding.title: Merge intervals
coding.prompt: Given a collection of intervals, merge all overlapping intervals.
coding.hint: Sort by interval start, then extend the last merged interval while ranges overlap.

concept.title: Sorted ranges merge in one pass
concept.summary: After sorting by start, every overlap is next to the range it overlaps. Extend the output’s last interval or start a new one.

steps.label: Sort by start
steps.detail: Order the ranges so the next possible overlap is always nearby.

steps.label: Extend an overlap
steps.detail: [2,6] starts before [1,3] ends, so extend the output range to [1,6].

steps.label: Start a new range
steps.detail: [8,10] no longer overlaps [1,6]. Add it, then continue scanning.

coding.title: Top K frequent elements
coding.prompt: Return the k most frequent elements from an integer array. Any order is accepted.
coding.hint: Count first, then use a min heap of size k or bucket sort by frequency.

concept.title: Count first, keep only the best k
concept.summary: Frequency counting turns the array into candidates. A size-k min heap keeps the k strongest candidates as you scan.

steps.label: Count values
steps.detail: Count each unique number once before ranking.

steps.label: Keep k candidates
steps.detail: Keep the two highest-frequency numbers. If the heap grows past k, remove its smallest frequency.

steps.label: Return the winners
steps.detail: The heap contains the most frequent values; order does not matter for this prompt.

coding.title: Product except self
coding.prompt: Return an array where each position is the product of all other input elements, without using division.
coding.hint: Build prefix products in one pass and suffix products in a second pass.

concept.title: Combine products from both sides
concept.summary: For each position, multiply everything before it by everything after it. Two passes avoid division and handle zero values naturally.

steps.label: Prefix pass
steps.detail: Store the product of all values to the left of each index.

steps.label: Suffix pass
steps.detail: Walk from right to left, multiplying each prefix by the running product on its right.

steps.label: Combine
steps.detail: The prefix and suffix products give the product of every other element.

coding.title: Valid parentheses
coding.prompt: Determine whether a string of brackets is valid and properly nested.
coding.hint: Push opening brackets. Each closing bracket must match the most recent opening bracket.

concept.title: The stack remembers the last opening bracket
concept.summary: A closing bracket must match the most recent opener. Last in, first out makes a stack a natural fit.

steps.label: Read openers
steps.detail: Push each opening bracket onto the stack.

steps.label: Match the closer
steps.detail: The next ] matches the top of the stack, so pop it.

steps.label: Finish clean
steps.detail: Every closer matched and the stack is empty, so the expression is valid.

coding.title: Binary tree levels
coding.prompt: A binary tree is encoded in level order with nulls for missing nodes. Return the values grouped by level.
coding.hint: Use a queue and process exactly the number of nodes currently in the queue for each level.

concept.title: A queue visits the tree one level at a time
concept.summary: Breadth-first search processes the earliest discovered node first. Capture the queue length before each level so children belong to the next one.

steps.label: Start at root
steps.detail: The root is the first and only node in the queue.

steps.label: Visit this level
steps.detail: Remove 3 and enqueue its children 9 and 20.

steps.label: Continue breadth-first
steps.detail: Process the captured queue length, then repeat for the next level.

systems.title: Design a rate limiter
systems.scenario: Design a rate limiter for a public API handling 1M requests per second across multiple regions.
guide: Clarify whether limits are per user, key, or endpoint and what consistency is required.
Compare token bucket, leaky bucket, and sliding window; explain the tradeoffs.
Choose an enforcement point and discuss distributed counters, hot keys, regional behavior, and cache.
Cover failure policy, abuse resistance, observability, and how you would test limits at scale.

systems.title: Design a URL shortener
systems.scenario: Design a URL shortener that supports 100M new links each month and fast global redirects.
guide: Estimate read/write volume and define expiry, custom aliases, and redirect requirements.
Choose an ID generation strategy and data model; discuss collision handling.
Cover cache, database partitioning, global reads, and consistency.
Add abuse controls, analytics, and operational metrics.

systems.title: Design a notification service
systems.scenario: Design a service that delivers email, push, and SMS notifications to 50M users.
guide: Clarify delivery guarantees, priority, preferences, and per-channel constraints.
Design queues and workers with deduplication, retries, and backoff.
Discuss provider failures, rate limits, ordering, and dead-letter handling.
Define delivery observability, privacy controls, and capacity planning.

systems.title: Design a news feed
systems.scenario: Design a personalized home feed for 100M users with low-latency reads.
guide: Compare fan-out on write and fan-out on read, including celebrity accounts.
Describe ranking inputs, pagination, and feed freshness.
Design cache keys and invalidation while managing hot users.
Discuss storage growth, backfills, and feed quality metrics.

systems.title: Design a file storage service
systems.scenario: Design a cloud file service that syncs large files across devices and supports sharing.
guide: Separate file metadata from blob storage and define chunking and resumable upload.
Cover sync protocol, versioning, and concurrent edit conflicts.
Discuss sharing permissions, encryption, and link revocation.
Address durability, replication, quotas, and recovery.

systems.title: Design a metrics platform
systems.scenario: Design an internal metrics platform ingesting millions of data points per second.
guide: Clarify query patterns, freshness, retention, and cardinality limits.
Design buffered ingestion and a time-series storage layout.
Cover downsampling, aggregation, alerting, and backpressure.
Define isolation, cost controls, and service-level objectives.

systems.title: Design a job scheduler
systems.scenario: Design a distributed scheduler that runs millions of delayed and recurring jobs.
guide: Define timing precision, recurring job semantics, and delivery guarantees.
Discuss sharding, safely claiming jobs, and worker coordination.
Cover retries, dead letters, fairness, and hot partitions.
Address clock issues, observability, and operational recovery.

trend.title: From copilots to agentic workflows
trend.intro: Production agent engineering centers on measuring outcomes, tracing the full run, and keeping permissions and escalation paths clear.

points.title: Measure outcomes
points.text: Build task-specific evaluations into the development loop.

points.title: Observe the whole run
points.text: Trace tool calls, latency, cost, and handoffs.

points.title: Keep control legible
points.text: Bound permissions and define human escalation paths.

trend.readingSummary: Agent reliability is becoming an engineering discipline: evaluation, observability, and deliberate context design show up alongside model choice.
